Data Encryption Standard

Purpose and scope

This standard sets out how Alderbridge encrypts data held on a laptop or tablet. It applies to every Alderbridge-issued laptop and, newly reflected in this version's title, every issued tablet.

Policy statement

All Alderbridge laptops, and as before any issued tablet, use full-disk encryption enabled by IT before issue, protecting resident and staff data if a device is lost or stolen.

Definitions

**Full-disk encryption** encryption applied to an entire device's storage, so data cannot be read without the correct credentials, even if the physical storage is removed. **Device** covers both a laptop and an issued tablet under this version's renamed title; the underlying laptop requirement is unchanged from the previous version. **Enabled before issue** the requirement that encryption is confirmed active before a device reaches its user, never enabled retrospectively after use has begun.

Enable full-disk encryption on every laptop and issued tablet before it is issued to a staff member.

Verify encryption status as part of IT's pre-issue checklist, never issuing a device where this check has not passed.

Report a device suspected to have been issued without encryption enabled to IT immediately for urgent remediation.

Include encryption verification for both laptops and tablets in the annual device audit across all sites.

Mobile Device Management Policy

*Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2024. Withdraws the bring-your-own-device allowance for roles accessing resident health records; those roles now require a company-issued device only.*

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group manages mobile devices, including phones and tablets used to access resident records or care systems. It applies to every company-issued device and, for roles not accessing resident health records, every personal device approved for work use.

Policy statement

A mobile device that can access resident information is managed to the same security standard as an office computer, and for roles accessing resident health records specifically, only a company-issued device is now used, so that resident data remains protected wherever it is accessed from.

Definitions

**Company-issued device** a phone or tablet provided by Alderbridge and enrolled in the mobile device management system before use. **Approved personal device** a staff member's own phone or tablet, approved by IT and enrolled in the same system, now used only under a bring-your-own-device arrangement for roles not accessing resident health records. **Enrolment** the process of registering a device in the mobile device management system, applying required security settings before it can access any Alderbridge system.

Roles and responsibilities

**IT** enrols every device, company-issued or approved personal, before it is permitted to access any Alderbridge system, confirms which roles require a company-issued device under this version, and can remotely wipe a lost or stolen device. **The device user** reports a lost or stolen device to IT immediately and never disables the security settings the enrolment process applies. **The registered manager** approves which staff roles require mobile access to resident systems at their site and confirms which of those roles now require a company-issued device.

Assessing severity: the four-factor test

The Data Protection Lead assesses every breach against four factors: the type of data involved (special
category health data is treated as inherently higher risk than, for example, a name and appointment time
alone); the volume of data and number of individuals affected; how quickly and completely containment
was achieved; and the likely consequence for the individuals affected if the data were misused, ranging
from mere inconvenience to genuine physical, financial or reputational harm — this structured four-factor

the next.

Post-incident review process

Following any Tier 2 or higher incident, IT leads a post-incident review within 10 working days of resolution, completing the lessons-learned appendix template and documenting any change needed to this plan.

Detailed containment procedure by system type

Containment differs meaningfully depending on the affected system's nature. For a single endpoint device, IT disconnects it from the network immediately without powering it off, preserving volatile memory evidence. For a server-based system, IT isolates the affected network segment at the switch level rather than the individual server, since lateral spread may not yet be fully visible. For a cloud-hosted system, IT contacts the cloud provider's own security team in parallel with internal containment, since containment options there often require provider-side action.

Detailed containment procedure by system type (continued)

For a network device itself, IT does not simply power-cycle it, since this can both destroy evidence and, in some scenarios, trigger a malicious payload configured to activate on restart. For a shared care records system spanning multiple sites, IT considers whether a partial, site-by-site isolation is sufficient rather than isolating the entire system nationally, weighing containment benefit against operational disruption to unaffected sites.

Evidence preservation

Before any remediation step that could alter or destroy evidence, IT takes a forensic image or detailed log export of the affected system where practicable, since a later insurance claim, regulatory enquiry, or law enforcement investigation may depend on evidence a hurried remediation step could otherwise destroy.

Communicating with residents and families during a cyber incident

Where a cyber incident genuinely affects a resident-facing system or resident data, the registered manager at an affected site is briefed by IT and, working with the Communications function, provides residents and families with a clear, honest, appropriately reassuring update, following the same honesty principle as the Duty of Candour Guidance, adapted to a cyber security context.

Working with external specialist support

At Tier 3 or above, IT engages Alderbridge's retained external cyber security specialist firm, whose contact details and engagement terms are held centrally by IT and the cyber insurance provider, now formally coordinated with the insurance notification step this version introduces.

Cyber Incident Response Plan

Supersedes the version effective 1 October 2025. Adds a mandatory cyber insurance provider notification step, adds a formal post-incident lessons-learned appendix template, and requires Board Chair co-approval alongside the Chief Executive for any ransomware-related decision at Tier 4.

Purpose and scope

This plan sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected cyber security incident, including ransomware, a data breach, or unauthorised system access. It applies to every site and every system holding Alderbridge or resident data.

Policy statement

A cyber incident is contained, reported and recovered from quickly and in a coordinated way, classified against the four-tier severity model, with the insurance and governance safeguards this version adds for the most serious incidents.

Definitions

**Cyber incident** any suspected compromise of an Alderbridge system. **Containment** the immediate step of isolating an affected system to prevent further spread. **The Data Protection Officer (DPO)** assesses personal data breach implications within 12 hours. **Severity tier** one of four classifications (Tier 1 to Tier 4). **Cyber insurance provider notification** the new mandatory step, introduced in this version, notifying Alderbridge's cyber insurance provider at Tier 3 or above. **Board Chair co-approval** the new requirement, introduced in this version, for a Tier 4 ransomware-related decision.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** reports a suspected cyber incident to IT immediately. **IT** classifies severity, contains the affected system, and now notifies the cyber insurance provider at Tier 3 or above. **The DPO** assesses data breach implications within 12 hours. **The Chief Executive**, for a Tier 4 ransomware-related decision, now seeks Board Chair co-approval before proceeding, a new governance safeguard introduced in this version.

Personal Data Breach Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected or confirmed personal data
breach, under the UK GDPR's own breach-notification requirements. It applies to any incident involving
personal data — a lost device, a misdirected email, unauthorised access, or a genuine cyber incident —
regardless of how minor it initially appears.

Policy statement

Alderbridge treats a fast, honest internal report of a suspected breach as far more valuable than a delayed,
polished one, and this procedure is deliberately built around a very short internal reporting window, since
the regulatory 72-hour clock for a notifiable breach starts running from when Alderbridge becomes aware
of it, not from when the investigation concludes.

Definitions

**Personal data breach** a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss,
alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data. **Notifiable breach** a breach likely to
result in a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms, requiring notification to the Information Commissioner's
Office within 72 hours of Alderbridge becoming aware of it. **High-risk breach** a breach likely to result in
a high risk to individuals, additionally requiring the affected individuals themselves to be notified without
undue delay. **Containment** the immediate action taken to stop a breach continuing or worsening (for
example, recalling a misdirected email, or disabling a compromised account).

Roles and responsibilities

The employee** works only from an approved location, using only an Alderbridge-issued, encrypted device for any system requiring it. **The line manager** confirms the remote working arrangement is genuinely suitable for the role before it begins. **IT** provides the technical setup (VPN, secure access) needed for safe remote working.

1. Use only an Alderbridge-issued laptop with full-disk encryption to access the care records system or any other sensitive system remotely; personal devices are never used for this.
2. Work from your approved location; if you need to work from a different location (for example, travelling), agree this with your manager in advance.
3. Use a privacy screen and position your device so screen content is not visible to others in a shared or public space.
4. Lock your screen whenever you step away from your device, exactly as you would in the office.
5. Do not print sensitive documents at home unless genuinely necessary, and if you must, dispose of them via confidential shredding rather than household waste.
6. Report a lost or stolen device immediately, exactly as you would report a data breach, since a device out of your possession is treated with the same urgency wherever it was last used.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a genuinely urgent situation requires briefly accessing a system from an unapproved location (for example, responding to an emergency while travelling), staff use only the approved secure method available (for example, the mobile app for messaging, never the full care records system on an unencrypted device) and inform their manager afterward.

Local and regional variations

This guidance applies specifically to Central Support Office roles where remote working is a genuine option; it does not apply to care-facing roles, which are inherently site-based.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Flexible Working Policy (governing how a remote arrangement is agreed), the Data Encryption Standard (governing the device-level control), and the IT Acceptable Use Policy (setting the wider security standard).

Application updates and patching

Every enrolled device applies operating system and application updates automatically through the mobile device management system, with a device that falls more than 14 days behind the required update level automatically restricted from accessing resident information until it is brought current; this check now applies to a larger proportion of the fleet given the withdrawal of the personal-device allowance for health-record roles.

Device replacement and end-of-life handling

A company-issued device reaching the end of its supported life is replaced through IT rather than continuing in use once security updates are no longer available for it, and the old device is factory-reset and its enrolment removed before any onward disposal or reuse; a personal device withdrawn from health-record use under this version follows the same factory-reset and de-enrolment step before it is returned to ordinary personal use.

Closing note

Mobile access to resident information brings real convenience for staff working away from a fixed desk, and narrowing the bring-your-own-device allowance in this version exists to keep that convenience safe specifically where the data involved is most sensitive, not to remove it everywhere.

Remote Working: Keeping Data Secure

Purpose and scope

These guidance notes set out how Central Support Office staff working under an agreed flexible arrangement keep Alderbridge data secure while working remotely. They apply to any employee approved to work away from an Alderbridge site.

Policy statement

Remote working is fully supported where a role allows it, provided the same data security standard applies regardless of location; working from home is never treated as a lower-security environment by default, but staff take specific, practical steps to make it genuinely as secure as an office setting.

Definitions

**Approved remote location** the employee's own home, or another location specifically agreed with their manager, as distinct from an unapproved public location. **Full-disk encryption** the device-level security control described in the Data Encryption Standard, required on any device used remotely. **VPN** a secure connection method used to access Alderbridge systems remotely where required.

Roles and responsibilities

**The employee** works only from an approved location, using only an Alderbridge-issued, encrypted device for any system requiring it. **The line manager** confirms the remote working arrangement is genuinely suitable for the role before it begins. **IT** provides the technical setup (VPN, secure access) needed for safe remote working.

4 incident extends beyond a single working day, IT and the Chief Executive's office issue a brief internal update to affected sites at least once daily, even where there is no material change to report, since an absence of communication during a prolonged incident tends to generate uncertainty that a short, honest update prevents more effectively than silence.

Reviewing this plan's own effectiveness after a real incident

Following any genuine Tier 3 or Tier 4 incident, the Board reviews not only the specific incident's own handling but whether this plan itself, including the insurance notification step and Board co-approval requirement, held up as intended, distinct from the routine post-incident review IT leads.

Vendor and platform-specific considerations

Alderbridge's core systems span several different software vendors and hosting arrangements, each with its own incident notification process and support escalation route; IT maintains a current reference sheet of each vendor's own emergency contact and typical response time commitment, since assuming a generic response time across every vendor risks under- or over-estimating how quickly external support can realistically be engaged during a genuine incident.

Remote and home working considerations

A staff member who works remotely, such as a Central Support Office role, follows the same reporting standard as a site-based colleague, using their own approved device and secure connection; a remote worker's own home network is not treated as a controlled Alderbridge environment, and this plan's containment steps for a remote worker's device rely more heavily on remote isolation capability than the physical network disconnection available on site.

Closing note

A fast, coordinated response to a cyber incident protects resident data and care continuity, and the insurance notification and Board-level co-approval added in this version exist to make sure the most serious incidents also receive the financial and governance safeguards their consequence genuinely warrants.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates both new controls. A staff member scans a resident's care plan to email, now authenticating with their PIN first, a new step this version adds; separately, when an old multifunction printer is replaced, IT completes a full data wipe of its internal storage before it leaves the site, since many modern printers store a surprising amount of scanned document history internally that a simple factory reset does not always fully clear.

Frequently asked questions

**Why was PIN authentication extended to scan-to-email?** A review found scan-to-email carried the same misdirection risk as printing, but without the PIN control print already had; extending it closes that gap. **Why does a printer need a data wipe when it is replaced?** Many printers store recent scan and print history internally, which would otherwise leave resident data on a device Alderbridge no longer controls.

Training and competency

Staff are shown how to use PIN-authenticated scan-to-email as part of general induction, and IT staff are trained on the end-of-life wipe procedure.

Approval and review history

This guidance was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 March 2024, this version took effect 1 March 2026 superseding the earlier version, and is due for review in March 2027.

Closing note

Closing the gap between convenience and confidentiality at every stage, from printing to scanning to eventual disposal, is what this guidance exists to do, and this version extends that protection to two points the previous version had not yet covered.

Why cyber insurance notification was added

A review of a near-miss Tier 3 incident found the insurance provider was notified only after recovery was already underway, by which point some options the policy offered, such as specialist negotiation support, were less useful than if engaged from the outset; mandatory notification at Tier 3 and above closes that gap.

Why Board Chair co-approval was added for Tier 4

A Tier 4 ransomware decision carries organisation-wide financial and reputational consequence beyond what any single individual should decide alone; requiring Board Chair co-approval alongside the Chief Executive adds a second, independent perspective to the most consequential decision this plan ever requires.

matter considered under the Disciplinary Procedure given the security risk created, illustrating that this
policy distinguishes proportionately between trivial personal use and a genuine security risk rather than
treating every deviation identically.

**Can I check personal email on my work computer?** Yes, within the reasonable personal use allowance,
provided it does not involve installing anything or storing Alderbridge data in a personal account. **What
happens if I forget my password?** Contact the IT service desk for a reset; never ask a colleague to log in
on your behalf, even temporarily, and never write your password down where others could see it. **Am I
monitored while using Alderbridge systems?** IT may monitor system use for security and safeguarding
purposes, proportionately and in line with data protection law, rather than continuously reviewing every
individual's activity without cause.

Training and competency

All staff complete IT acceptable use and phishing awareness training at induction and refresher training
annually, per the Mandatory Training Matrix.

Monitoring and compliance

IT reviews security incidents and policy exceptions quarterly, reporting significant findings to the Chief

that team.

Record keeping and retention

security investigation and demonstrating this policy's own practical enforcement over time.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group protects a staff member working alone, including a community visit and a single-staffed night shift. It applies to every community-visiting role and every single-staffed night-shift role.

Policy statement

A lone worker is issued a device with a panic button, GPS location and, for a newly issued device from this version onward, an automatic no-movement alert, paired with a mandatory check-in call and a now clearly defined escalation protocol if a check-in is missed.

2. Take immediate containment action within your own ability to do so (for example, recalling a misdirected

Why Board Chair co-approval was added for Tier 4

A Tier 4 ransomware decision carries organisation-wide financial and reputational consequence beyond what any single individual should decide alone; requiring Board Chair co-approval alongside the Chief Executive adds a second, independent perspective to the most consequential decision this plan ever requires.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates both new safeguards together. A Tier 4 ransomware incident affects the medication administration system network-wide. IT notifies the cyber insurance provider within hours as this version now requires, and when a ransom demand is received, the Chief Executive and Board Chair jointly review the external specialist advice before confirming the decision not to pay, a decision now formally co-approved rather than resting with the Chief Executive alone.

Frequently asked questions

**Does the insurance provider need to be told about a Tier 1 or Tier 2 incident?** No, mandatory notification applies at Tier 3 and above; a lower-tier incident may still be reported at IT's discretion if genuinely relevant. **What happens if the Board Chair is unavailable during a Tier 4 incident?** The Vice Chair provides co-approval in their place, following the same governance principle of an independent second perspective.

Training and competency

IT staff and senior leadership complete incident response training covering the four-tier model, insurance notification triggers, and the Tier 4 co-approval process.

Monitoring and compliance

Every cyber incident is logged with its severity tier and reviewed by IT and the DPO, with insurance notifications and lessons-learned appendices reported to the Board quarterly.

Record keeping and retention

Incident logs, severity classifications, insurance notifications and lessons-learned appendices are retained per the Records Retention Schedule.

Beyond the individual breach's own resolution, the Data Protection Lead reviews breach data quarterly for
any recurring type or cause, and a genuinely recurring pattern (for example, repeated misdirected emails
to a similarly named recipient) triggers a specific process or system change — for example, a mandatory
confirmation step before sending to an external address — rather than each individual recurrence simply
being logged and closed without addressing why it keeps happening.

Distinguishing a breach from an ordinary IT fault

Not every IT problem is a data breach; a system outage that prevents access to data, with no evidence
anyone unauthorised accessed or exfiltrated it, is handled under the IT Outage Contact Tree rather than
this procedure, though the Data Protection Lead is still briefed and remains alert to any sign the outage's
underlying cause might also have a data protection dimension that only becomes apparent as IT's own

A suspected breach discovered outside normal office hours is reported to the on-call manager, who
contacts the Data Protection Lead directly rather than the report waiting until the next working day, since

happened at a less convenient time.

Purpose and scope

Policy statement

Site keys or access cards are issued to permanent staff from their first day, the previous 4-week waiting period having been removed, logged in the key register, and every key and access card must now be returned on an employee's last working day.

Definitions

**Key register** the log recording every key or access card issued, to whom, and when, and now its confirmed return date. **First-day issue** the new standard replacing the previous 4-week qualifying period. **Leaver return** the new requirement that every key and access card is returned before final pay is released.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** authorises a key or access card issue from a staff member's first day, and confirms return on their last working day before final pay is released. **Facilities** cuts a key or programs an access card and updates the key register, now including the return date. **The staff member** keeps their key or access card secure, reports a lost one immediately, and returns it on their last working day.

Appendix: the 72-hour clock at a glance

For quick reference: the clock starts when Alderbridge becomes aware of the breach, not when the
investigation concludes; internal reporting within 1 hour of discovery gives the Data Protection Lead the
maximum possible time within that window to investigate properly and, where required, notify the ICO with
a genuinely complete, accurate assessment rather than a rushed, incomplete one submitted only to beat
the deadline.

Breaches involving a third-party data processor

Where a breach occurs at a third-party data processor holding Alderbridge data (for example, a payroll
provider), the processor's own contractual obligation to notify Alderbridge without undue delay is relied on,
but the Data Protection Lead also proactively checks in with key processors periodically, since the 72-hour
clock for Alderbridge's own notification obligation still runs from when Alderbridge itself becomes aware,
which can be later than when the processor's own breach actually occurred if the processor is slow to tell
Alderbridge.

Extended frequently asked questions

**What if the breach involves a former employee's data rather than a current one?** The same procedure
applies in full; a former employee's data remains protected personal data for as long as Alderbridge holds
it. **Can a breach be assessed as low risk simply because the recipient is another Alderbridge employee
rather than an external party?** No — an internal misdirection can still be a genuine breach, particularly for
special category health data, and is assessed on the actual risk to the individual concerned, not assumed
low risk purely because it stayed within the organisation. **Is a physical break-in and theft of paper records
treated the same as a digital breach?** Yes — the same assessment and notification process applies
regardless of whether the compromised data was digital or physical.

example

They lock the screen first, even though they expect to be back within a minute, since a brief absence is exactly the kind of moment an unlocked screen creates unnecessary risk.

Frequently asked questions

**Can a password manager be used to store an Alderbridge system password?** Yes, using the Alderbridge-approved password manager specifically; a personal, unapproved tool is not used for this purpose. **What happens if a staff member suspects their account has been accessed by someone else?** They contact IT immediately, who resets access and investigates, following the Cyber Incident Response Plan if warranted.

Training and competency

All staff receive password and account security guidance at induction, refreshed annually alongside wider cyber awareness training.

Multi-factor authentication

Where a system offers multi-factor authentication, this is enabled and used rather than relying on a password alone, since a password can be guessed or exposed in a way a second, device-based factor makes much harder for an attacker to bypass.

Closing note

A personal, strong password kept confidential protects far more than the individual account it belongs to, and this guidance exists to make that simple habit consistent across every system.

A key safe is installed only after property-owner consent, resident or representative agreement where applicable, and a recorded risk assessment. Each safe has a unique register entry linked to the address without exposing the code itself.

The responsible manager reviews continuing need, authorised recipients and physical condition at least annually and after a tenancy, care-package or risk change. When the safe is no longer required it is removed or disabled promptly, keys are returned and access records are closed. Personal Data Breach Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected or confirmed personal data
breach, under the UK GDPR's own breach-notification requirements. It applies to any incident involving
personal data — a lost device, a misdirected email, unauthorised access, or a genuine cyber incident —
regardless of how minor it initially appears.

Policy statement

Alderbridge treats a fast, honest internal report of a suspected breach as far more valuable than a delayed,
polished one, and this procedure is deliberately built around a very short internal reporting window, since
the regulatory 72-hour clock for a notifiable breach starts running from when Alderbridge becomes aware
of it, not from when the investigation concludes.

Definitions

**Personal data breach** a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss,
alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data. **Notifiable breach** a breach likely to
result in a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms, requiring notification to the Information Commissioner's
Office within 72 hours of Alderbridge becoming aware of it. **High-risk breach** a breach likely to result in
a high risk to individuals, additionally requiring the affected individuals themselves to be notified without
undue delay. **Containment** the immediate action taken to stop a breach continuing or worsening (for
example, recalling a misdirected email, or disabling a compromised account).

Roles and responsibilities

Backup testing and verification

IT performs a scheduled test restoration of a sample backup on a regular cycle, confirming both that the backup file itself is intact and that the restoration process actually produces a working system, rather than discovering a problem only at the point of a genuine incident.

Third-party and supplier risk

A cyber incident does not always originate within an Alderbridge-controlled system; a supplier or third-party provider with its own access to Alderbridge data or systems represents a genuine risk if that supplier's own security is weaker than Alderbridge's own standard. Before granting a supplier system access, IT assesses the supplier's own security practice at a level proportionate to the access being granted, and a supplier holding significant access is required to notify Alderbridge promptly of any security incident on their own side that could affect Alderbridge data, mirrored in the relevant supplier contract terms.

Coordinating with a supplier during an incident

Where a supplier notifies Alderbridge of an incident on their own side, or where Alderbridge's own investigation traces an incident's origin to a supplier system, IT treats this with the same urgency as an internally-originating incident, applying the same severity tier classification and engaging the supplier's own incident response team as part of the coordinated response.

Physical security as a cyber consideration

A cyber incident is not always purely digital in origin; an unattended, unlocked workstation, a discarded document containing a system password, or an unchallenged unfamiliar person in a server room area can each provide the starting point for a compromise just as effectively as a phishing email. This plan treats physical security awareness as a genuine part of the cyber security picture rather than an entirely separate concern.

Purpose and scope

Policy statement

Definitions

**3-2-1 principle** at least three copies of data, on two different media types, with one copy off-site.

introduced in this version, of the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time, distinct from the RTO's

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how every accident, incident, near miss, medication error and property damage event
is reported, investigated and learned from at Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every site and every
person present — staff, people supported, visitors and contractors.

Policy statement

Alderbridge treats thorough incident reporting as one of its most important safety tools, and actively
encourages reporting even where an event seems minor, since a genuine safety culture depends on
seeing the full picture, not only the events serious enough to be impossible to overlook.

Definitions

**Incident** any unplanned event that caused or could have caused harm or damage. **Near miss** an
event that could have caused harm but did not, on this occasion. **RIDDOR-reportable incident** an
incident meeting the specific statutory threshold requiring notification to the Health and Safety Executive.
**Root cause** the underlying, systemic reason an incident occurred, as distinct from its immediate,
surface-level cause.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** witnessing or discovering an incident reports it the same shift using the
appropriate form. **The registered manager** reviews every incident at their site, escalating a
RIDDOR-reportable or otherwise serious incident to the Health and Safety Lead immediately. **The Health
and Safety Lead** coordinates cross-site trend analysis and reports to the quarterly Health and Safety
Committee.

1. Report every accident, incident and near miss using the appropriate form (the Accident and Incident
Report Form, Safeguarding Referral Form, or Medication Error Report Form as applicable) within 24
hours, regardless of how minor it seems.

2. Take any immediate action needed to make the situation safe before completing the paperwork, since
first aid and safety always come before documentation.

3. The registered manager reviews every report the same or next working day, identifying whether any

Extended frequently asked questions

**If I'm off sick, do I still accrue annual leave?** Yes — annual leave continues to accrue during any period of sickness absence, in the same way as during active employment. **What if I disagree with occupational health's assessment of my fitness to return?** Discuss this with HR, who can arrange a further opinion or explore a modified return plan; the assessment informs the decision but is not applied rigidly without regard to your own account of how you are actually feeling. **Is there a limit to how much company sick pay I can receive in a year?** Yes, set out in your contract of employment and varying by length of service; once company sick pay is exhausted, statutory sick pay continues for as long as you remain eligible under current legislation. **Can I be asked to attend a return-to-work discussion by phone if I'm still recovering?** The discussion is normally held in person on your first day back, but where genuinely necessary can be arranged differently; the purpose (support, not box-ticking) matters more than the specific format.

How trigger points are calculated in practice

HR calculates trigger points using a rolling 12-month window measured backward from the most recent absence, not a fixed calendar year, so that an occasion from 13 months ago naturally drops out of the calculation without needing to be manually excluded, and every occasion within the current rolling window counts regardless of whether it happened at the very start or the very end of that window; this rolling approach is explained to every employee at induction, since a fixed calendar-year approach would otherwise create an artificial reset each January that does not reflect the underlying pattern being monitored.

A worked example illustrates the immutable backup's purpose. During a simulated ransomware exercise,

sophisticated ransomware attack can specifically target and encrypt a standard backup alongside the

cannot be altered even in that scenario. **What is the difference between RTO and RPO?** RTO is how
quickly a system is restored; RPO is how much data loss, measured in time, is acceptable — a
nightly-backed-up system has an RPO of roughly 24 hours since up to a day's data could be lost if the
incident occurs just before that night's backup.

Where a manual handling incident occurs, the subsequent review distinguishes explicitly between an equipment failure (which triggers an immediate equipment check across the site, not only the specific item involved) and a technique deviation (which triggers a refresher and, where appropriate, a wider look at whether the training itself needs updating), since conflating the two risks either an unaddressed equipment fault recurring or an individual being unfairly blamed for what was actually an equipment problem.

Manual handling during an emergency evacuation

The Fire Safety Policy's own PEEP arrangements take precedence during a genuine evacuation, meaning a person may be moved using whatever method their PEEP specifies for evacuation specifically, which can differ from their everyday MHRA where a faster, evacuation-specific method (for example, an evacuation sledge down a stairwell) is what the PEEP requires; staff are trained to recognise this is a deliberate, planned difference between the two documents, not a contradiction to resolve in the moment.

Closing note on culture

Alderbridge treats a member of staff raising a concern about a manual handling technique or piece of equipment as a positive contribution to safety, never as a complaint to be managed defensively, since the staff actually performing a technique every day are often the first to notice a genuine problem with it long before an audit or a formal review would otherwise catch it.

A final note on consistency across the organisation

The same MHRA format, the same equipment standard, and the same training curriculum apply across all five sites, so that a resident moving between Alderbridge homes, or a staff member covering a shift at an unfamiliar site, encounters a genuinely consistent approach rather than five subtly different local conventions that happen to share the same policy title.

sparse_candidates.chunk_text:
Quality Lead review whether the control measures in place are genuinely working — for example, whether new cases keep appearing despite enhanced cleaning, which would suggest the transmission route has not been correctly identified — rather than mechanically continuing the same measures for the outbreak's full duration regardless of whether the case trend suggests they are having the intended effect.

Supporting residents' wellbeing during restricted communal activity

Where communal activities are restricted during an outbreak, the activities coordinator adapts the Activities and Wellbeing Programme Policy's own offer to smaller, in-room or cohort-specific activity rather than simply suspending meaningful engagement altogether for the outbreak's duration, since prolonged isolation carries its own genuine wellbeing cost that must be weighed against, not simply overridden by, the infection-control benefit of restriction.

Distinguishing an outbreak from a single, isolated infection

A single case of a transmissible infection, with no second case within the 48-hour window, is managed under everyday infection control practice rather than this procedure's outbreak-specific measures; the registered manager still monitors for a possible second case for a reasonable period afterward, but does not apply enhanced cleaning, cohorting or visiting restriction on the strength of one case alone, since doing so would impose the cost of an outbreak response without the actual outbreak having occurred.

Record of decisions, not only case counts

Beyond the daily case log, the registered manager keeps a brief, dated record of every significant decision made during an outbreak — when enhanced cleaning began, when cohorting was applied, when it was relaxed — since this decision log, not only the raw case numbers, is what a later review or regulatory enquiry actually needs to understand whether the response was timely and proportionate.

Coordinating with GP practices and community health services

Where an outbreak involves a condition requiring clinical input beyond Alderbridge's own staff (for example, confirming a diagnosis or advising on treatment for affected residents), the registered manager coordinates directly with the residents' own GP practices rather than each resident's care being managed in isolation from the wider outbreak response, ensuring clinical advice and Alderbridge's own infection-control measures are working from the same understanding of what is actually happening at the site.

Purpose and scope

This standard sets out how Alderbridge encrypts data held on a laptop or tablet. It applies to every Alderbridge-issued laptop and, newly reflected in this version's title, every issued tablet.

Policy statement

All Alderbridge laptops, and as before any issued tablet, use full-disk encryption enabled by IT before issue, protecting resident and staff data if a device is lost or stolen.

Definitions

**Full-disk encryption** encryption applied to an entire device's storage, so data cannot be read without the correct credentials, even if the physical storage is removed. **Device** covers both a laptop and an issued tablet under this version's renamed title; the underlying laptop requirement is unchanged from the previous version. **Enabled before issue** the requirement that encryption is confirmed active before a device reaches its user, never enabled retrospectively after use has begun.

Enable full-disk encryption on every laptop and issued tablet before it is issued to a staff member.

Verify encryption status as part of IT's pre-issue checklist, never issuing a device where this check has not passed.

Report a device suspected to have been issued without encryption enabled to IT immediately for urgent remediation.

Include encryption verification for both laptops and tablets in the annual device audit across all sites.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

Cyber Incident Response Plan

Supersedes the version effective 1 October 2025. Adds a mandatory cyber insurance provider notification step, adds a formal post-incident lessons-learned appendix template, and requires Board Chair co-approval alongside the Chief Executive for any ransomware-related decision at Tier 4.

Purpose and scope

This plan sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected cyber security incident, including ransomware, a data breach, or unauthorised system access. It applies to every site and every system holding Alderbridge or resident data.

Policy statement

A cyber incident is contained, reported and recovered from quickly and in a coordinated way, classified against the four-tier severity model, with the insurance and governance safeguards this version adds for the most serious incidents.

Definitions

**Cyber incident** any suspected compromise of an Alderbridge system. **Containment** the immediate step of isolating an affected system to prevent further spread. **The Data Protection Officer (DPO)** assesses personal data breach implications within 12 hours. **Severity tier** one of four classifications (Tier 1 to Tier 4). **Cyber insurance provider notification** the new mandatory step, introduced in this version, notifying Alderbridge's cyber insurance provider at Tier 3 or above. **Board Chair co-approval** the new requirement, introduced in this version, for a Tier 4 ransomware-related decision.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** reports a suspected cyber incident to IT immediately. **IT** classifies severity, contains the affected system, and now notifies the cyber insurance provider at Tier 3 or above. **The DPO** assesses data breach implications within 12 hours. **The Chief Executive**, for a Tier 4 ransomware-related decision, now seeks Board Chair co-approval before proceeding, a new governance safeguard introduced in this version.

Personal Data Breach Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected or confirmed personal data
breach, under the UK GDPR's own breach-notification requirements. It applies to any incident involving
personal data — a lost device, a misdirected email, unauthorised access, or a genuine cyber incident —
regardless of how minor it initially appears.

Policy statement

Alderbridge treats a fast, honest internal report of a suspected breach as far more valuable than a delayed,
polished one, and this procedure is deliberately built around a very short internal reporting window, since
the regulatory 72-hour clock for a notifiable breach starts running from when Alderbridge becomes aware
of it, not from when the investigation concludes.

Definitions

**Personal data breach** a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss,
alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data. **Notifiable breach** a breach likely to
result in a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms, requiring notification to the Information Commissioner's
Office within 72 hours of Alderbridge becoming aware of it. **High-risk breach** a breach likely to result in
a high risk to individuals, additionally requiring the affected individuals themselves to be notified without
undue delay. **Containment** the immediate action taken to stop a breach continuing or worsening (for
example, recalling a misdirected email, or disabling a compromised account).

Roles and responsibilities

Mobile Device Management Policy

*Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2024. Withdraws the bring-your-own-device allowance for roles accessing resident health records; those roles now require a company-issued device only.*

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group manages mobile devices, including phones and tablets used to access resident records or care systems. It applies to every company-issued device and, for roles not accessing resident health records, every personal device approved for work use.

Policy statement

A mobile device that can access resident information is managed to the same security standard as an office computer, and for roles accessing resident health records specifically, only a company-issued device is now used, so that resident data remains protected wherever it is accessed from.

Definitions

**Company-issued device** a phone or tablet provided by Alderbridge and enrolled in the mobile device management system before use. **Approved personal device** a staff member's own phone or tablet, approved by IT and enrolled in the same system, now used only under a bring-your-own-device arrangement for roles not accessing resident health records. **Enrolment** the process of registering a device in the mobile device management system, applying required security settings before it can access any Alderbridge system.

Roles and responsibilities

**IT** enrols every device, company-issued or approved personal, before it is permitted to access any Alderbridge system, confirms which roles require a company-issued device under this version, and can remotely wipe a lost or stolen device. **The device user** reports a lost or stolen device to IT immediately and never disables the security settings the enrolment process applies. **The registered manager** approves which staff roles require mobile access to resident systems at their site and confirms which of those roles now require a company-issued device.

Reviewing this plan's own effectiveness after a real incident

Following any genuine Tier 3 or Tier 4 incident, the Board reviews not only the specific incident's own handling but whether this plan itself, including the insurance notification step and Board co-approval requirement, held up as intended, distinct from the routine post-incident review IT leads.

Vendor and platform-specific considerations

Alderbridge's core systems span several different software vendors and hosting arrangements, each with its own incident notification process and support escalation route; IT maintains a current reference sheet of each vendor's own emergency contact and typical response time commitment, since assuming a generic response time across every vendor risks under- or over-estimating how quickly external support can realistically be engaged during a genuine incident.

Remote and home working considerations

A staff member who works remotely, such as a Central Support Office role, follows the same reporting standard as a site-based colleague, using their own approved device and secure connection; a remote worker's own home network is not treated as a controlled Alderbridge environment, and this plan's containment steps for a remote worker's device rely more heavily on remote isolation capability than the physical network disconnection available on site.

Closing note

A fast, coordinated response to a cyber incident protects resident data and care continuity, and the insurance notification and Board-level co-approval added in this version exist to make sure the most serious incidents also receive the financial and governance safeguards their consequence genuinely warrants.

Purpose and scope

This standard sets out how Alderbridge encrypts data held on a laptop or tablet. It applies to every Alderbridge-issued laptop and, newly reflected in this version's title, every issued tablet.

Policy statement

All Alderbridge laptops, and as before any issued tablet, use full-disk encryption enabled by IT before issue, protecting resident and staff data if a device is lost or stolen.

Supersedes the version effective 1 October 2025. Adds a mandatory cyber insurance provider notification step, adds a formal post-incident lessons-learned appendix template, and requires Board Chair co-approval alongside the Chief Executive for any ransomware-related decision at Tier 4.

Purpose and scope

This plan sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected cyber security incident, including ransomware, a data breach, or unauthorised system access. It applies to every site and every system holding Alderbridge or resident data.

Policy statement

A cyber incident is contained, reported and recovered from quickly and in a coordinated way, classified against the four-tier severity model, with the insurance and governance safeguards this version adds for the most serious incidents.

Definitions

**Cyber incident** any suspected compromise of an Alderbridge system. **Containment** the immediate step of isolating an affected system to prevent further spread. **The Data Protection Officer (DPO)** assesses personal data breach implications within 12 hours. **Severity tier** one of four classifications (Tier 1 to Tier 4). **Cyber insurance provider notification** the new mandatory step, introduced in this version, notifying Alderbridge's cyber insurance provider at Tier 3 or above. **Board Chair co-approval** the new requirement, introduced in this version, for a Tier 4 ransomware-related decision.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** reports a suspected cyber incident to IT immediately. **IT** classifies severity, contains the affected system, and now notifies the cyber insurance provider at Tier 3 or above. **The DPO** assesses data breach implications within 12 hours. **The Chief Executive**, for a Tier 4 ransomware-related decision, now seeks Board Chair co-approval before proceeding, a new governance safeguard introduced in this version.

Report a suspected cyber incident to IT immediately.

IT classifies the incident against the four-tier severity model within 30 minutes.

Personal Data Breach Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected or confirmed personal data
breach, under the UK GDPR's own breach-notification requirements. It applies to any incident involving
personal data — a lost device, a misdirected email, unauthorised access, or a genuine cyber incident —
regardless of how minor it initially appears.

Policy statement

Alderbridge treats a fast, honest internal report of a suspected breach as far more valuable than a delayed,
polished one, and this procedure is deliberately built around a very short internal reporting window, since
the regulatory 72-hour clock for a notifiable breach starts running from when Alderbridge becomes aware
of it, not from when the investigation concludes.

Definitions

**Personal data breach** a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss,
alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data. **Notifiable breach** a breach likely to
result in a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms, requiring notification to the Information Commissioner's
Office within 72 hours of Alderbridge becoming aware of it. **High-risk breach** a breach likely to result in
a high risk to individuals, additionally requiring the affected individuals themselves to be notified without
undue delay. **Containment** the immediate action taken to stop a breach continuing or worsening (for
example, recalling a misdirected email, or disabling a compromised account).

Roles and responsibilities

Mobile Device Management Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group manages mobile devices, including phones and tablets used to access resident records or care systems. It applies to every company-issued device and, for roles not accessing resident health records, every personal device approved for work use.

Policy statement

A mobile device that can access resident information is managed to the same security standard as an office computer, and for roles accessing resident health records specifically, only a company-issued device is now used, so that resident data remains protected wherever it is accessed from.

Definitions

**Company-issued device** a phone or tablet provided by Alderbridge and enrolled in the mobile device management system before use. **Approved personal device** a staff member's own phone or tablet, approved by IT and enrolled in the same system, now used only under a bring-your-own-device arrangement for roles not accessing resident health records. **Enrolment** the process of registering a device in the mobile device management system, applying required security settings before it can access any Alderbridge system.

Roles and responsibilities

**IT** enrols every device, company-issued or approved personal, before it is permitted to access any Alderbridge system, confirms which roles require a company-issued device under this version, and can remotely wipe a lost or stolen device. **The device user** reports a lost or stolen device to IT immediately and never disables the security settings the enrolment process applies. **The registered manager** approves which staff roles require mobile access to resident systems at their site and confirms which of those roles now require a company-issued device.

Reviewing this plan's own effectiveness after a real incident

Following any genuine Tier 3 or Tier 4 incident, the Board reviews not only the specific incident's own handling but whether this plan itself, including the insurance notification step and Board co-approval requirement, held up as intended, distinct from the routine post-incident review IT leads.

Vendor and platform-specific considerations

Alderbridge's core systems span several different software vendors and hosting arrangements, each with its own incident notification process and support escalation route; IT maintains a current reference sheet of each vendor's own emergency contact and typical response time commitment, since assuming a generic response time across every vendor risks under- or over-estimating how quickly external support can realistically be engaged during a genuine incident.

Remote and home working considerations

A staff member who works remotely, such as a Central Support Office role, follows the same reporting standard as a site-based colleague, using their own approved device and secure connection; a remote worker's own home network is not treated as a controlled Alderbridge environment, and this plan's containment steps for a remote worker's device rely more heavily on remote isolation capability than the physical network disconnection available on site.

Closing note

A fast, coordinated response to a cyber incident protects resident data and care continuity, and the insurance notification and Board-level co-approval added in this version exist to make sure the most serious incidents also receive the financial and governance safeguards their consequence genuinely warrants.

the next.

Reviewing this plan's own effectiveness after a real incident

Following any genuine Tier 3 or Tier 4 incident, the Board reviews not only the specific incident's own handling but whether this plan itself, including the insurance notification step and Board co-approval requirement, held up as intended, distinct from the routine post-incident review IT leads.

Vendor and platform-specific considerations

Alderbridge's core systems span several different software vendors and hosting arrangements, each with its own incident notification process and support escalation route; IT maintains a current reference sheet of each vendor's own emergency contact and typical response time commitment, since assuming a generic response time across every vendor risks under- or over-estimating how quickly external support can realistically be engaged during a genuine incident.

Remote and home working considerations

A staff member who works remotely, such as a Central Support Office role, follows the same reporting standard as a site-based colleague, using their own approved device and secure connection; a remote worker's own home network is not treated as a controlled Alderbridge environment, and this plan's containment steps for a remote worker's device rely more heavily on remote isolation capability than the physical network disconnection available on site.

Closing note

A fast, coordinated response to a cyber incident protects resident data and care continuity, and the insurance notification and Board-level co-approval added in this version exist to make sure the most serious incidents also receive the financial and governance safeguards their consequence genuinely warrants.

Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. 'Laptop encryption' renamed to 'Device encryption' to reflect coverage of tablets as well as laptops — no requirement changed for laptops specifically.

This standard sets out how Alderbridge encrypts data held on a laptop or tablet. It applies to every Alderbridge-issued laptop and, newly reflected in this version's title, every issued tablet.

Policy statement

All Alderbridge laptops, and as before any issued tablet, use full-disk encryption enabled by IT before issue, protecting resident and staff data if a device is lost or stolen.

Personal Data Breach Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected or confirmed personal data
breach, under the UK GDPR's own breach-notification requirements. It applies to any incident involving
personal data — a lost device, a misdirected email, unauthorised access, or a genuine cyber incident —
regardless of how minor it initially appears.

Policy statement

Alderbridge treats a fast, honest internal report of a suspected breach as far more valuable than a delayed,
polished one, and this procedure is deliberately built around a very short internal reporting window, since
the regulatory 72-hour clock for a notifiable breach starts running from when Alderbridge becomes aware
of it, not from when the investigation concludes.

Definitions

**Personal data breach** a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss,
alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data. **Notifiable breach** a breach likely to
result in a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms, requiring notification to the Information Commissioner's
Office within 72 hours of Alderbridge becoming aware of it. **High-risk breach** a breach likely to result in
a high risk to individuals, additionally requiring the affected individuals themselves to be notified without
undue delay. **Containment** the immediate action taken to stop a breach continuing or worsening (for
example, recalling a misdirected email, or disabling a compromised account).

notified one.

type of misdirected email), feeding into training or process changes rather than being treated as a one-off,

Approval and review history

This procedure was originally approved by the Chief Executive on 25 May 2025 and is scheduled for its

Appendix: the 72-hour clock at a glance

For quick reference: the clock starts when Alderbridge becomes aware of the breach, not when the
investigation concludes; internal reporting within 1 hour of discovery gives the Data Protection Lead the
maximum possible time within that window to investigate properly and, where required, notify the ICO with
a genuinely complete, accurate assessment rather than a rushed, incomplete one submitted only to beat
the deadline.

Breaches involving a third-party data processor

Where a breach occurs at a third-party data processor holding Alderbridge data (for example, a payroll
provider), the processor's own contractual obligation to notify Alderbridge without undue delay is relied on,
but the Data Protection Lead also proactively checks in with key processors periodically, since the 72-hour
clock for Alderbridge's own notification obligation still runs from when Alderbridge itself becomes aware,
which can be later than when the processor's own breach actually occurred if the processor is slow to tell
Alderbridge.

Extended frequently asked questions

**What if the breach involves a former employee's data rather than a current one?** The same procedure
applies in full; a former employee's data remains protected personal data for as long as Alderbridge holds
it. **Can a breach be assessed as low risk simply because the recipient is another Alderbridge employee
rather than an external party?** No — an internal misdirection can still be a genuine breach, particularly for
special category health data, and is assessed on the actual risk to the individual concerned, not assumed
low risk purely because it stayed within the organisation. **Is a physical break-in and theft of paper records
treated the same as a digital breach?** Yes — the same assessment and notification process applies
regardless of whether the compromised data was digital or physical.

residents' names jotted in it count as a breach?** Potentially yes — any loss of personal data, however
seemingly minor the format, is reported and assessed rather than dismissed based on the format it was
recorded in. **Will I get in trouble for reporting my own mistake?** No — the same principle that applies to
safeguarding and incident reporting applies here: raising your own honest mistake promptly is treated
entirely differently from concealing one.

outcome.

A final practical reminder for every member of staff

You do not need to know the details of this whole procedure to do the one thing that matters most: if someone asks what personal data Alderbridge holds about them, tell the Data Protection Lead the same day, and let the rest of this procedure do its job from there — you do not need to assess authority, redaction, or timescale yourself; that is precisely what the Data Protection Lead exists to do once told, and doing so promptly is the single most useful contribution any individual member of staff can make to this whole procedure working as intended, more useful by far than trying to assess the request's validity or scope yourself before passing it on, since that assessment genuinely requires the Data Protection Lead's own specific training and judgement, built up through handling many such requests across every part of the organisation over time, in a way a well-intentioned but untrained colleague simply could not reliably replicate on a single isolated occasion, however carefully and conscientiously they genuinely tried to help with the very best of intentions.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates fast containment limiting a breach's impact. A member of staff at Central

distribution list. Realising the error within minutes, they immediately report it to the Data Protection Lead,
who recalls the email where technically possible and contacts every recipient directly asking them to delete

Post-breach review and organisational learning

Beyond the individual breach's own resolution, the Data Protection Lead reviews breach data quarterly for

to a similarly named recipient) triggers a specific process or system change — for example, a mandatory

Distinguishing a breach from an ordinary IT fault

Not every IT problem is a data breach; a system outage that prevents access to data, with no evidence
anyone unauthorised accessed or exfiltrated it, is handled under the IT Outage Contact Tree rather than

investigation progresses.

A suspected breach discovered outside normal office hours is reported to the on-call manager, who
contacts the Data Protection Lead directly rather than the report waiting until the next working day, since

happened at a less convenient time.

Personal Data Breach Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected or confirmed personal data
breach, under the UK GDPR's own breach-notification requirements. It applies to any incident involving
personal data — a lost device, a misdirected email, unauthorised access, or a genuine cyber incident —
regardless of how minor it initially appears.

Policy statement

Alderbridge treats a fast, honest internal report of a suspected breach as far more valuable than a delayed,
polished one, and this procedure is deliberately built around a very short internal reporting window, since
the regulatory 72-hour clock for a notifiable breach starts running from when Alderbridge becomes aware
of it, not from when the investigation concludes.

Definitions

**Personal data breach** a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss,
alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data. **Notifiable breach** a breach likely to
result in a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms, requiring notification to the Information Commissioner's
Office within 72 hours of Alderbridge becoming aware of it. **High-risk breach** a breach likely to result in
a high risk to individuals, additionally requiring the affected individuals themselves to be notified without
undue delay. **Containment** the immediate action taken to stop a breach continuing or worsening (for
example, recalling a misdirected email, or disabling a compromised account).

Roles and responsibilities

, the Data Protection Lead informs Alderbridge's own insurer and,
where the breach is significant, seeks legal advice on any further obligation or exposure, treating these as
parallel tracks running alongside, not instead of, the core regulatory and individual-notification obligations
this procedure primarily governs.

Breach severity thresholds used for internal escalation

This procedure uses three internal severity bands to decide who is informed and how quickly, beyond the
regulatory notification decision itself: a low-severity breach (contained quickly, minimal data, no special
category information) is handled by the Data Protection Lead with a routine report to the next scheduled
compliance update; a medium-severity breach (special category data involved, or containment took longer
than expected) is escalated to the Chief Executive within 24 hours; a high-severity breach (large volume,
vulnerable individuals significantly affected, or a systemic cause suggesting other similar exposure may
exist) triggers immediate Chief Executive and Board Chair notification regardless of time of day.

Testing the breach response itself

The Data Protection Lead runs an occasional simulated breach scenario, similar in spirit to a fire drill, to
confirm the internal reporting chain and the Data Protection Lead's own investigation and notification
process work smoothly under realistic time pressure, rather than the process being tested for the first time
during a genuine, high-stakes incident.

Final note on why speed matters as much as thoroughness

A breach response that is eventually thorough but slow to start is far more damaging than one that starts
reporting and containing within minutes even if the full investigation takes longer to complete, since the
actual harm to an affected individual accumulates during every hour a breach remains uncontained, which
is precisely why this procedure's own internal reporting window is measured in a single hour rather than a
working day.

Coordinating with communications and reputation management

For any breach significant enough to carry a realistic risk of media or public attention, the Chief Executive
coordinates the organisation's external communications directly, ensuring the same honest,
plain-language standard described above for individual notification is maintained publicly too, rather than a
defensive public position being adopted that contradicts what affected individuals have themselves already
been told privately.

Lawful basis for key processing activities

Care record processing relies primarily on the lawful basis of vital interests and the performance of a task
carried out in the substantial public interest for special category health data, alongside the person's own
consent where they are able to give it meaningfully. Employment record processing relies on the
performance of the employment contract and compliance with legal obligations. CCTV footage relies on
legitimate interests in the safety and security of people supported, staff and visitors, as set out in the CCTV
Policy. Marketing communications, where they occur at all, rely on explicit consent, never legitimate
interests, and that consent can be withdrawn at any time.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Personal data may be shared without the data subject's consent, or even without their knowledge in a
genuine emergency, where doing so is necessary to protect someone's vital interests — for example,
sharing a resident's allergy information with a paramedic during a medical emergency — but this exception
is used narrowly, for the specific emergency at hand, never as a general licence to share more broadly.

Data Encryption Standard

Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. 'Laptop encryption' renamed to 'Device encryption' to reflect coverage of tablets as well as laptops — no requirement changed for laptops specifically.

Purpose and scope

This standard sets out how Alderbridge encrypts data held on a laptop or tablet. It applies to every Alderbridge-issued laptop and, newly reflected in this version's title, every issued tablet.

Policy statement

All Alderbridge laptops, and as before any issued tablet, use full-disk encryption enabled by IT before issue, protecting resident and staff data if a device is lost or stolen.

Definitions

**Full-disk encryption** encryption applied to an entire device's storage, so data cannot be read without the correct credentials, even if the physical storage is removed. **Device** covers both a laptop and an issued tablet under this version's renamed title; the underlying laptop requirement is unchanged from the previous version. **Enabled before issue** the requirement that encryption is confirmed active before a device reaches its user, never enabled retrospectively after use has begun.

Enable full-disk encryption on every laptop and issued tablet before it is issued to a staff member.

Verify encryption status as part of IT's pre-issue checklist, never issuing a device where this check has not passed.

Report a device suspected to have been issued without encryption enabled to IT immediately for urgent remediation.

Include encryption verification for both laptops and tablets in the annual device audit across all sites.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This standard works alongside the Mobile Device Management Policy (governing the wider device management framework encryption sits within) and the Cyber Incident Response Plan (relevant where a lost device's encryption status affects the incident response).

Supersedes the version effective 1 October 2025. Adds a mandatory cyber insurance provider notification step, adds a formal post-incident lessons-learned appendix template, and requires Board Chair co-approval alongside the Chief Executive for any ransomware-related decision at Tier 4.

Purpose and scope

This plan sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected cyber security incident, including ransomware, a data breach, or unauthorised system access. It applies to every site and every system holding Alderbridge or resident data.

Policy statement

A cyber incident is contained, reported and recovered from quickly and in a coordinated way, classified against the four-tier severity model, with the insurance and governance safeguards this version adds for the most serious incidents.

Definitions

**Cyber incident** any suspected compromise of an Alderbridge system. **Containment** the immediate step of isolating an affected system to prevent further spread. **The Data Protection Officer (DPO)** assesses personal data breach implications within 12 hours. **Severity tier** one of four classifications (Tier 1 to Tier 4). **Cyber insurance provider notification** the new mandatory step, introduced in this version, notifying Alderbridge's cyber insurance provider at Tier 3 or above. **Board Chair co-approval** the new requirement, introduced in this version, for a Tier 4 ransomware-related decision.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** reports a suspected cyber incident to IT immediately. **IT** classifies severity, contains the affected system, and now notifies the cyber insurance provider at Tier 3 or above. **The DPO** assesses data breach implications within 12 hours. **The Chief Executive**, for a Tier 4 ransomware-related decision, now seeks Board Chair co-approval before proceeding, a new governance safeguard introduced in this version.

Report a suspected cyber incident to IT immediately.

IT classifies the incident against the four-tier severity model within 30 minutes.

Containment differs meaningfully depending on the affected system's nature. For a single endpoint device, IT disconnects it from the network immediately without powering it off, preserving volatile memory evidence. For a server-based system, IT isolates the affected network segment at the switch level rather than the individual server, since lateral spread may not yet be fully visible. For a cloud-hosted system, IT contacts the cloud provider's own security team in parallel with internal containment, since containment options there often require provider-side action.

For a network device itself, IT does not simply power-cycle it, since this can both destroy evidence and, in some scenarios, trigger a malicious payload configured to activate on restart. Data Backup and Recovery Policy

Supersedes the version effective 1 September 2025. Adds an immutable, air-gapped backup copy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group backs up and can recover its core systems and data. It
applies to every core system holding Alderbridge or resident data.

Policy statement

Every core system is backed up nightly following the 3-2-1 principle, tested monthly, with a documented
recovery time objective, now supplemented by an immutable, air-gapped backup copy protecting against
ransomware, and a defined recovery point objective per system.

Definitions

**3-2-1 principle** at least three copies of data, on two different media types, with one copy off-site.
**Immutable backup** the new backup type, introduced in this version, that cannot be altered or deleted
even by an attacker with wide system access, protecting against ransomware that might otherwise encrypt
a standard, writable backup. **Recovery point objective (RPO)** the new documented measure,
introduced in this version, of the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time, distinct from the RTO's
focus on restoration speed.

Roles and responsibilities

**IT** runs the nightly backup process, the monthly test restoration, and now maintains the immutable
backup copy separately from standard backups. **A system owner** confirms both their system's RTO and
its new RPO are realistic and documented. **The IT Director** reviews test restoration outcomes and
immutable backup integrity monthly.

A data protection impact assessment (DPIA) is completed before Alderbridge introduces any new

Where Alderbridge occasionally sends a newsletter or event invitation to family members who have opted

specifically for the marketing purpose, can be withdrawn at any time through a clearly signposted method
in every communication sent, and withdrawing that consent never affects, or is ever perceived to affect,
the standard of care a resident receives — a boundary Alderbridge treats as absolute precisely because of

the police, or another care provider a resident is transferring to — is never actioned on the strength of the

A worked example illustrates the immutable backup's purpose. During a simulated ransomware exercise,

alongside the primary system in a genuine attack of this type; the immutable, air-gapped copy remains

Frequently asked questions

**Why was an immutable backup added when the 3-2-1 principle already existed?** A review found that a
sophisticated ransomware attack can specifically target and encrypt a standard backup alongside the
primary system if both are reachable from the same compromised network; an immutable, air-gapped copy
cannot be altered even in that scenario. **What is the difference between RTO and RPO?** RTO is how
quickly a system is restored; RPO is how much data loss, measured in time, is acceptable — a
nightly-backed-up system has an RPO of roughly 24 hours since up to a day's data could be lost if the
incident occurs just before that night's backup.
