Severity classification table

Tier	Description	Example	Response
Tier 1	Single device, no evidence of spread	One laptop displaying a suspicious prompt	IT service desk handles directly during normal hours
Tier 2	Single site affected, contained locally	A site's local network shows unusual traffic	IT escalates to the on-call IT lead; regional emergency contact engaged if out of hours
Tier 3	Multiple sites or a core system affected	A shared care records system shows signs of compromise	IT Director engaged; Business Continuity Plan considered; cyber insurance provider notified
Tier 4	Organisation-wide, or resident safety directly implicated	Ransomware affecting the medication administration system network-wide	Chief Executive and Board Chair engaged immediately; Business Continuity Plan activated; cyber insurance provider notified

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where an affected system is critical to immediate resident safety regardless of its formal severity tier, IT prioritises a safe manual fallback process alongside containment, treating the resident-safety implication as at least Tier 3, which also now triggers the cyber insurance notification step.

**On-call manager** the senior manager currently holding the on-call rota responsibility for a specific region. **Regional on-call number** one of three mobile numbers, one per region, replacing the previous single central number. **Weekly rota** the rotation within each region's own senior management team, each taking on-call responsibility for one week at a time.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any staff member** on shift calls their own region's on-call number for a genuine out-of-hours concern requiring senior management input. **The regional on-call manager** answers their region's number during their rota week and provides guidance or attends site as the situation requires. **HR** maintains each region's weekly rota and ensures every senior manager knows their upcoming on-call weeks well in advance.

Call your own region's on-call mobile number for any out-of-hours concern requiring senior management input; the previous single central number has been decommissioned and no longer connects.

Give a clear, concise account of the situation to the regional on-call manager who answers, including what has already been done.

Follow the on-call manager's guidance, or arrange for them to attend site if they judge this necessary.

Record the call and its outcome in the site's on-call log.

1. Enrol every device, company-issued or approved personal, in the mobile device management system before it accesses any Alderbridge system.
2. Any role accessing resident health records uses a company-issued device only; the previous bring-your-own-device allowance for these roles has been withdrawn.
3. A role not accessing resident health records may still use an approved personal device under the bring-your-own-device arrangement.
4. Report a lost or stolen device to IT immediately, at any hour, so a remote wipe can be triggered without delay.
5. Never disable, bypass or attempt to remove the security settings the enrolment process applies, including screen lock and remote wipe capability.
6. Use only Alderbridge-approved applications to access resident information; a personal messaging or file-sharing application is never used to send resident data.
7. Return a company-issued device to IT within five working days of leaving Alderbridge, or of no longer requiring mobile access.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a genuinely urgent situation requires a health-record-accessing staff member to use a device temporarily while their own company-issued device is repaired, IT issues a loan company-issued device rather than permitting a personal device exception, since the bring-your-own-device route is no longer available to this role category at all.

Local and regional variations

Community-visiting staff at Willow Bank, who access resident health records during visits, now carry a company-issued device without exception under this version, whereas office-based staff at smaller sites in roles not accessing health records may still use an approved personal device under the bring-your-own-device arrangement.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Data Protection and Information Governance Policy (the wider standard this device-level control supports) and the Acceptable Use Policy (governing how any device, mobile or otherwise, is used).

Extended worked example: a lost unencrypted device

A worked example illustrates a more serious breach. A community support worker's personal, unencrypted
phone, on which the lone-worker app was installed alongside some informal notes about client visits, is
lost during a shift. This is reported immediately, and the Data Protection Lead assesses it as notifiable
given the special category health data potentially exposed on an unencrypted device, notifies the ICO
within 72 hours, and, since the risk to the specific clients whose information may have been exposed is
genuinely elevated, notifies those individuals directly with practical guidance; separately, this incident
triggers an immediate review under the Mobile Device Management Policy of why an unencrypted
personal device was being used to store any client information at all, closing the underlying practice gap
rather than treating the incident as resolved once the notification obligations are met.

Breach severity communicated internally, not only externally

Beyond the ICO and affected-individual notifications, the Data Protection Lead briefs the Chief Executive
and, for a high-risk breach, the Board on what happened and why, in language that is equally honest
internally as any external communication would be, since a culture of internal minimisation about a
breach's true severity undermines the organisation's ability to learn from it, even where the external, legally
required notifications are handled correctly.

Interim measures pending full investigation

Where a full investigation will genuinely take some time, the Data Protection Lead puts interim measures
in place immediately where a plausible, proportionate one exists — for example, temporarily suspending a
specific system's remote access pending confirmation of how a credential was compromised — rather
than waiting for the complete investigation to conclude before taking any protective action at all.

answer_parts.text: The device-control is implemented via the organisation's mobile device management — devices must be enrolled in the mobile device management system — and IT is responsible for classifying incidents against the four-tier severity model.
The Data Protection Officer (DPO) must assess whether the incident is a personal data breach within 12 hours.

The out-of-hours route now uses regional on-call mobile numbers (one per region) so staff call their region's on-call mobile number outside normal hours; additionally, the procedures reference contacting the regional IT emergency contact for out-of-hours support at Tier 2 or higher.
